distinguishing_features: A bonded low-modulus polyurethane/polyurea elastomer layer is applied to the wetted impeller surfaces rather than changing ball charge or mill speed.
The layer reduces erosive damage by viscoelastic deformation, longer contact time, and attenuation of transmitted impact stress instead of by lowering impact frequency or velocity.
The impeller-specific 2-3 mm coating, adhesion primer, and trim machining preserve hydraulic clearances while changing surface compliance.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce mass loss of a centrifugal slurry pump impeller caused by high-velocity hard-particle impacts while maintaining the existing pump geometry and operating envelope.
parsed.viable_reason: A bonded 2-3 mm PU/polyurea layer is a practical impeller coating and can dissipate fine-particle impact energy, and its benefit can be checked by comparative slurry mass-loss tests.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 2 only lowers impact energy flux through ball-size and speed changes and gives no teaching or suggestion to use a compliant dissipative elastomer surface layer on a slurry-pump impeller.
